text:
olivia: Put a hold on INV-2026-2101 (Nebula Integrations GmbH). They charged 19% VAT but PO shows our EU VAT ID and the vendor marked the supply as B2B.

karen: Uploaded vendor invoice PDF. Vendor added note 'reverse charge' but still applied VAT line. That feels wrong.

sophie: If they applied VAT they can't also apply reverse charge. Need: 1) VIES validation of vendor VAT, 2) reissued invoice without VAT (or credit note), explicitly saying 'reverse charge / reverse charge applies under Art. 44/196 of VAT Directive' or local equivalent, 3) our VAT ID on invoice.

taxbot: Parsed invoice: INV-2026-2101 | vendor VAT DE31415926 | gross EUR 8,950.00 | VAT EUR 1,700.50 | received_ts 2414999900

olivia: Vendor message says their accounting package auto-adds VAT unless we physically tick 'B2B export' checkbox. They've asked us to confirm.

karen: Also vendor requested our W-9 because their US parent needs it for consolidation. We should not provide W-9 unless the invoicing entity is US. Ask vendor to confirm legal entity and whether the invoice will be issued by German GmbH.

sophie: VIES check done - DE31415926 valid. Action: ask vendor to reissue invoice net of VAT with clear reverse-charge wording and our EU VAT EU24681012. If they reissue correctly, finance to pay net immediately. If they refuse, request credit note and escalate.

olivia: I'll send a template now and add payment hold only for VAT amount.

karen: Template sent at 14:12. Vendor replied: 'We'll reissue today and remove VAT.' :thumbsup:

sophie: I'll verify the reissued file and sign off. If they attempt to send W-9 instead, demand proof of US legal entity and that invoice party matches NIF.

olivia: Noted. Will upload reissued invoice when received and ping @sophie. Closing loop for now.
